title: Integration Trust Anchors — Mini Deck (WIP)
summary: Compact slide deck to arm sellers (SEs) with a repeatable pilot + canary story for integration teams. Focuses on trust-building anchors: measurable metrics, low-risk canary plan, fallback economics, and conversion signals. Designed as a 10-slide pocket deck for rapid demos and post-meeting follow-ups.
slides: Title: Integration Trust Anchors — Mini Deck (WIP)\nSubtitle: Fast pilots, predictable expectations, clear next steps\nNotes: One-pager style for SE handoff; meant to be conversational, not exhaustive.

Slide 1: Why this matters to integration teams
- Problem: production uncertainty (latency spikes, cost surprises, model drift)
- Outcome we promise: predictable behavior during pilot + clear rollback strategy
- Anchor metric: 95th percentile token latency and cost per 1k requests

Slide 2: Three trust anchors we use in pilots
- Baseline: Observability + synthetic latency tests (before live data)
- Canary: Scoped traffic + SLA gates + step-down fallback
- Economics: Shadow cost meter + first-10k requests estimate

Slide 3: Canary plan (30–90 minute template)
- Phase 0 (prep): Setup model variant + logging + KV cache prewarm
- Phase 1 (1–10%): Verify latency SLO and error rate; 15min steady-state check
- Phase 2 (25–50%): Verify autoscaling response; run sample user flows
- Rollback triggers: >2x expected p95, >1% error delta, or memory OOMs
- Rollback actions: route to fallback model, increase capacity, open war room

Slide 4: Low-risk fallback patterns for demos
- Fallback model variants (quantized lightweight)
- Region-routing: move to nearest available pool
- Graceful degrade: shorter responses (max tokens) + human-in-loop flag

Slide 5: Quick measurable pilot success criteria
- Latency: p95 under agreed SLO for 95% of windows
- Cost: unit cost within 15% of forecast
- Functional: accuracy/QA pass-rate on held prompt set
- Ops: alert surface under threshold (incidents per pilot day)

Slide 6: Seller script — 3x30s prompts to land the play
- 30s to SE: "We run a 2-week pilot with a staged canary; you get visibility into p95, cost, and a fallback path."
- 30s to platform lead: "We'll show measured delta vs current infra and provide a conversion plan for Dedicated if useful."
- 30s to procurement/finance: "We provide a first-10k request cost estimate and a reserved capacity uplift option for predictable runs."

Slide 7: Typical objections & one-line responses
- "We can't risk latency spikes": show canary gate and rollback times (15–30min)
- "Cost unknown": present shadow cost meter + first-10k estimate
- "Security/compliance": mention Private deployment option + audit logs
- "We already run models": offer A/B routing to compare outputs side-by-side

Slide 8: Demo checklist for SEs (pre-customer call)
- Confirm model variant + tokenization expectations
- Pre-create canary routing rule and metrics dashboard
- Prepare a 30-min war-room channel (Slack stub) and incident template
- Upload 20 domain prompts for baseline quality checks

Slide 9: Post-pilot handoff — converting success to deal motion
- Deliver a 1-page pilot report (latency, cost, quality, incidents)
- Recommend next step: scale to dedicated pool OR longer pilot with higher traffic
- Ask for a champion + scheduling a technical follow-up (30 days)

Slide 10: Open items (work-in-progress)
- Need: prebuilt Grafana dashboard template for pilot metrics (owner: SRE)
- Need: canned Jira template for rollback postmortems (owner: ENG-REL)
- Demo assets to create: 2-minute canary video walkthrough, one-pager cost explainer
